MINUTES
  ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  DECEMBER 13, 2023

CHAIR STEGURA called the meeting of the Environmental Advisory Committee Meeting of the
City of Rolling Hills Estates at 7:00 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL

COMMITTEE MEMBERS PRESENT:  Stegura, Bain, Chuang, Nicklas, Schachter,
  Schmidt, Uppal

COMMITTEE MEMBERS ABSENT:  Bacinski, Larson

STAFF MEMBERS PRESENT:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

NONE

4.  AUDIENCE ITEMS/ORAL COMMUNICATION ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

5.  DISCUSSION ITEMS

A.  PLASTIC POLLUTION PREVENTION

  Whitney Berry, Senior Planner, provided a presentation summarizing the staff report,
  which included a brief overview SB54 – the Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging
  Producer Responsibility Act.

  Senior Planner Berry stated that staff recommends that the EAC direct staff: 1) To review
  local polystyrene policies and return at a future meeting to present this information; and
  2) To prepare a draft ordinance for a city-wide polystyrene ban and return at a future
  meeting to discuss.

  CHAIR STEGURA added that SB54 was successfully carried by Senator Ben Allen after
  failing to get the bill signed initially, he was able to convince people to shift the cost to
  producers rather than consumers, and the bill was signed into law.

  Director Naughton provided a brief explanation on the Sustainability Element and General
  Plan.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER NICKLAS asked how the cost is going from the consumer to the
  producer. Senior Planner Berry stated that there are specific targets for packaging material
  content to be recyclable and it is the responsibility of the producers to find a way to achieve
  this.

  Craig Cadwallader, Surf Rider Foundation, provided a presentation on minimizing plastic
  single-use products and compostable single-use or reusable products.

  Elizabeth Sala, League of Women Voters PVP, provided a presentation on the harmful
  effects of plastics and polystyrene products. She also explained how businesses have
  shifted to using reusable products.

  Mr. Cadwallader spoke on some of the impacts of polluting items that were improperly
  disposed of, where the leading items are cigarettes and plastic drinking bottles. He
  provided information on some of the changes that restaurants have made to move toward
  using reusable food serving dishes.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER NICKLAS asked what businesses will use to serve food. Ms. Sala
  stated that they could use dishes that can be washed and reused.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER NICKLAS stated that businesses may be concerned with the cost
  of making the change from disposable products to reusable or compostable products. Mr.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  1
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 13, 2023
   Cadwallader stated that he and other agencies have done cost comparison studies; the
  cost to change from polystyrene to a compostable material is minimal and businesses can
  also obtain grants to help with the cost.

  Mr. Cadwallader stated that they are proposing an ordinance to ban poly-styrene products.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN inquired if there are already businesses in the community
  who are already using this approach to their business and who are willing to come forward.

  Mr. Cadwallader stated that he would like to go directly to the PVP Chamber of Commerce.
  He will provide the proposed draft ordinance to staff.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER NICKLAS,

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO FURTHER INVESTIGATE THIS ITEM AND
  COLLABORATE WITH MR. CADWALLADER, SURF RIDER FOUNDATION TO
  GET THE FACTS AND PRESENT THIS ITEM TO THE CITY COUNCIL.ALSO,
  TO SURVEY BUSINESSES IN THE CITY ON THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE.

  There being no objection, CHAIR STEGURA so ordered.

B.  CONSIDERATION OF A PROHIBITION OF GASOLINE-POWERED LEAF BLOWERS

  Director Naughton provided a brief overview of AB1346, which will phase out the sale of
  gas powered small off-road engines and will go into effect on January 1, 2024. There is
  nothing in the ordinance for already existing equipment. There are rebate programs for
  residents and landscape businesses.

  Director Naughton stated that there are some challenges for the landscape businesses
  with the cost to replace the equipment even with the rebate program as well as the battery
  life for electric equipment.

  Director Naughton stated that there has only been one complaint regarding leaf-blowers,
  and it had to do with their use at a commercial property before construction hours.
  However, there are serious health impacts from the use of gas leaf blowers. She added
  that in the studies that staff reviewed regarding noise, there is not much difference in the
  decibel, but they do run at a different frequency.

  Director Naughton stated that staff recommends that the committee discuss the issue and
  direct staff whether an ordinance should be drafted to recommend to City Council.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked about information on how neighboring cities have
  enacted a ban on gas powered leaf blowers and their mechanism for educating their
  residents on the change. CHAIR STEGURA added that staff provide how this will be
  enforced. COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked for data on the cost difference of using
  gas-powered and electric-powered equipment.

  Director Naughton agreed to inquire with neighboring cities on enactment on the gas-
  powered leaf blowers ban, and with the city’s landscaping company for the cost. This item
  will be discussed at the next Environmental Advisory Committee meeting.

6.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

A.  SOUTH BAY ENERGY AND CLIMATE RECOGNITION PROGRAM

  CHAIR STEGURA stated that the City of Rolling Hills Estates was awarded gold level
  recognition for its contributions to sustainability and the environment.

B.  ARTIFICIAL TURF

  CHAIR STEGURA stated that Governor Brown signed an ordinance that prohibited local
  jurisdictions from installing synthetic grass. Governor Newsom reversed this, and local
  jurisdictions can now prohibit synthetic grass.

  CHAIR STEGURA asked the committee about considering a ban on the installation of new
  artificial turf. The reason for banning this would be the forever chemicals in production of
  the artificial turf and chemicals that may pollute runoff.

 ENVIRONMENTAL ADVISORY COMMITTEE MEETING
  2
 MINUTES, DECEMBER 13, 2023
   COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN asked if staff can look into the consequences in using
  plastic ground barrier used for landscape.

  The committee directed staff to gather more information and bring it back to be discussed
  at the next Environmental Advisory Committee meeting.

7.  COMMITTEE ITEMS/FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  Director Naughton stated that the CPA has a grant program to provide technical assistant
  for the development of reach codes. This is a way for project applicants to go above and
  beyond the requirements of the building code in regard to energy efficiency. Staff would
  be pursuing a voluntary program. Staff will bring back more information about the program,
  the codes, and a letter of agreement for the city to participate in the program and move
  forward with the next steps.

  The next Environmental Advisory Committee meeting will be held on January 17, 2024 at
  7:00 p.m.

8.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

9.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIR STEGURA adjourned the meeting at 8:20 p.m. The next meeting will be held on January
17, 2024 at 7:00 p.m.
